about.title: Sounding out words with U and E
about.length_note: About 10 minutes fits this class: two new vowel sounds, a few words for each, then a short mixed practice. It is in two halves (U, then E), so you can stop for a rest after the U words and come back.

say.text: Hello {name}, and welcome to class six. Today we sound out words with two vowels: U and E. Go slowly. There is no rush and no wrong speed.

show.text: Sounding out words with U and E

say.text: First, the short U sound. It says 'uh', like the start of 'up'. Say it with me: uh, uh, uh.
Now the word sun. Three letters, three sounds. S says 'sss'. U says 'uh'. N says 'nnn'. Slide them together: sss-uh-nnn... sun.

show.text:
S = sss
U = uh
N = nnn
sun

say.text: Let's try two more. C, U, P: cuh-uh-puh... cup. B, U, S: buh-uh-sss... bus. Take your time with each one.
Let's check. Which of these words has the 'uh' sound in the middle?

ask.q: Which word has the 'uh' sound (short U) in the middle?
ask.why: Bus has the letter U in the middle, and U says 'uh'. Bed, pen and red all have E in the middle.

say.text: Well done. Now the short E sound. It says 'eh', like the start of 'egg'. Say it with me: eh, eh, eh.
Here are three E words. B, E, D: buh-eh-duh... bed. P, E, N: puh-eh-nnn... pen. R, E, D: rrr-eh-duh... red.
Picture a pen lying on a table. Which word says pen? Sound out each one if it helps.

show.text: A blue pen lying on a wooden table.

ask.why: P-E-N gives puh-eh-nnn, which is pen. The other words have a different middle or last letter.

say.text: U and E can feel close together. Keep them apart: U is 'uh' with a relaxed mouth. E is 'eh' with the mouth a little wider. Compare the words side by side.

show.text:
U says 'uh': sun, cup, bus
E says 'eh': bed, pen, red

say.text: Now a mixed practice with all five vowels. Look at each middle letter, then say its sound. A is 'a' as in cat. I is 'ih' as in sit. O is 'o' as in dog. U is 'uh' as in sun. E is 'eh' as in bed.
Last job: choose the right word for a picture. Look at the picture, sound out the choices one at a time, and pick the one that matches.

show.text: A bright yellow sun shining in a blue sky.

ask.why: S-U-N gives sss-uh-nnn, which is sun. The other words start with the same sound but have different middle letters.

say.text: One more. A picture of a bed with a blanket. You can sleep in it. Which word is it?

show.text: A bed with a soft blanket and a pillow.

ask.q: Which word matches the picture of a bed?
ask.why: B-E-D gives buh-eh-duh, which is bed. Check the middle letter: E says 'eh'.

say.text: Well done, {name}. You read sun, cup, bus, bed, pen and red. Rest now if you like. Next class we begin spelling by choosing letters.

show.text:
sun  cup  bus
bed  pen  red

notes.topic: Choosing a word for a picture
